headline: Independent restaurants define Ward 35's strength, thin park acreage its clearest gap.
summary:
Avondale, Logan Square, Irving Park and Hermosa sit inside a Northwest Side ward built around independent restaurants and bike-friendly spending, one that finishes 14th overall out of fifty, on a score of 51.1. Its restaurants skew independent rather than chain, the second-lowest chain share of the fifty, and its bars post some of the highest average ratings in the city. City infrastructure money backs that pattern up. The ward has put a larger share of its aldermanic menu funds into bike lanes, sidewalks, and street redesigns than all but three wards, and it spreads that money across more kinds of projects than most wards do.

The ward falls behind on green space and a couple of slower-moving city services. Park acreage per resident is among the lowest in the city, and only two wards are slower to close a rodent baiting request. Estimated adult loneliness runs higher than most of Chicago too, and the ward's dense permit parking zones point to a real parking squeeze. Council attendance tied to the ward's representation lands in the bottom five, though that figure blends more than one alderman's term across the 2023 boundary change. Ward 35 reads as a walkable stretch of the city with a strong restaurant and bar scene and real money going into biking and walking routes, even where green space and a couple of routine services have not kept pace.
reading_the_rankings:
Park Access lands at 48th out of 50, but that ranking is softer than it looks. A dozen other wards come within a similarly tight band of Ward 35's score, and this measure's citywide range runs a full eleven points, wider than most of the ward-level numbers here, so the real distance between Ward 35 and much of Chicago is smaller than 48th place implies.

The fourth-place rank on menu money spent on bike and pedestrian projects is tied to the ward's footprint as it stands today, redrawn in 2023, so it reads as one year's snapshot, not a running trend for a single continuous ward.

And the attendance figure, in the bottom five for the ward's representation, blends more than one alderman's term across that same 2023 boundary change, and it carries only medium confidence in the source's own grading.

news.headline: Construction Begins On Logan Square's Megamall Plaza
news.note: Work started on a new public plaza at the former Megamall site in Logan Square, with seating, a performance space, and a play area planned for completion by early next year.

news.headline: New Housing OK'd For Avondale, McKinley Park, Streeterville And Across From Johnny's Icehouse
news.note: City Council's zoning committee advanced an apartment and townhome development in Avondale at 3231-65 N. California Ave., part of nearly 300 housing units approved that day.

news.headline: Logan Square Homeless Encampment Being Cleared Ahead Of Plaza Construction
news.note: The last residents of a longtime encampment near the Logan Square monument relocated ahead of construction on the new public plaza there.
